summary: The Marshall Islands lets US citizens enter, live and work indefinitely without a visa under the Compact of Free Association, waives visas for 30 to 90 days for a moderate list of partner countries including Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Taiwan and the EU, and issues a paid visitor visa on arrival in Majuro to almost everyone else.

Republic of the Marshall Islands — entry requirements

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers aged 1 and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Standard routings via Honolulu, Guam or Nadi do not trigger it.

source.name: Republic of the Marshall Islands — health requirements

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not required for entry and is not checked. It is nonetheless close to essential: Majuro Hospital and the Ebeye clinic provide basic care only, dental and specialist services are minimal, and serious cases are flown to Honolulu or Guam. Confirm your policy covers air ambulance from a remote Pacific island, and diving cover if you plan wreck dives.

source.name: Republic of the Marshall Islands — entry requirements

onwardTicket.text: Visitors must show a confirmed onward or return ticket and where they will stay. With the island-hopper and Nauru Airlines services running only a few times a week, immigration expects a realistic departure date.

source.name: Republic of the Marshall Islands — entry requirements

proofOfFunds.text: No published minimum. Officers may ask visitors to show they can support themselves; carrying US dollars in cash is the practical answer, since card acceptance is patchy.

source.name: Republic of the Marshall Islands — entry requirements

declarations.name: Arrival Card and Customs Declaration
declarations.text: All arrivals complete a paper immigration arrival card and customs declaration, given out on the flight. It asks for your address in Majuro and your departure flight. The same details the immigration officer uses to set your stay.

source.name: Republic of the Marshall Islands — arrival procedures

notes: Quarantine rules cover fresh food, plants, seeds and soil. Declare anything organic, including fruit picked up on the island-hopper.
Firearms and ammunition are prohibited without prior authorization, and are taken seriously at Majuro's small airport.

Visiting Bikini, Enewetak, Rongelap and other atolls affected by the US nuclear testing program requires permission from the local atoll council or the national government — arrange it long before you arrive.

Kwajalein island hosts a US Army garrison and is not open to casual visitors: access needs US military sponsorship, separate from your RMI entry permission. Neighboring Ebeye is not restricted in the same way.

payments.text: The country uses the US dollar, which removes any exchange problem, but acceptance is the issue: a few hotels, the larger stores and dive operators in Majuro take cards, and ATMs exist in Majuro and Ebeye but can run out of notes. Outer atolls are entirely cash. Bring small US bills for the whole trip.

safety.text: Serious crime against visitors is uncommon and the islands are welcoming, with occasional petty theft and some alcohol-related trouble at night in Majuro and Ebeye. The practical risks dominate: very limited medical care, thin flight connections, no drinkable tap water, strong reef currents, and low-lying atolls exposed to king tides, flooding and drought.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Marshall Islands travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to April is the drier, breezier half of the year and the most comfortable time to travel; May to November brings heavier rain. The Marshalls sit at the eastern edge of the typhoon belt, so tropical storms are possible mainly late in the wet season.

tips.text: Under the Compact of Free Association, US citizens may enter the Marshall Islands and live and work there without a visa or time limit. You still need a valid passport and still complete the arrival card. The arrangement runs the other way too: Marshallese citizens may live and work in the United States.

Medical care is basic. Majuro Hospital handles routine emergencies, Ebeye has a clinic, and the outer atolls have health assistants only. Anything serious means a flight to Honolulu or Guam. Carry your own medications with prescriptions, and insurance that names medical evacuation.

Majuro is reached mainly by the United island-hopper between Honolulu and Guam and by Nauru Airlines from Brisbane, each running only a few times a week. A missed or canceled flight can cost you several days, so leave buffer time and never book a tight onward international connection.

Bikini, Enewetak, Rongelap and other atolls affected by the nuclear testing program are not casual destinations — visits need permission from the atoll council or the national government, and Bikini diving depends on a charter operating that season. Kwajalein island requires US military sponsorship, though Ebeye does not.

Do not drink the tap water. Most supply is rainwater catchment and droughts strain it. Stick to bottled or boiled water, and bring small-denomination US dollars, since ATMs are limited to Majuro and Ebeye and can be empty.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for the Marshall Islands?
faq.answer: US citizens do not. The Compact of Free Association lets them enter, live and work in the Marshall Islands indefinitely with just a valid passport. Citizens of a moderate list of partner countries, including Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Japan, Taiwan and most EU states, enter visa-free for 30 days, and citizens of Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia get longer under Micronesian arrangements. Everyone else can obtain a visitor visa on arrival in Majuro for a fee of about USD 50.

faq.question: How does the visa on arrival work?
faq.answer: It is issued at the immigration desk at Amata Kabua International Airport in Majuro against a passport valid six months, a confirmed onward ticket, accommodation details and a fee payable in US dollars cash. Bring the exact amount, as card payment is not reliable. The visa is normally valid for 30 days and can be extended at the Division of Immigration.

faq.question: How long can I stay in the Marshall Islands?
faq.answer: Thirty days is the standard grant for visa-free visitors and for visas issued on arrival, extendable at the Division of Immigration in Majuro up to around 90 days in total. US citizens under the Compact have no time limit at all.

faq.question: Can Americans work in the Marshall Islands under the Compact?
faq.answer: Yes. The Compact of Free Association gives US citizens the right to reside and be employed in the Marshall Islands without an immigration permit, which is why it functions more like freedom of movement than a visa waiver. Employers may still require local registration or professional licensing, so check with them before you start.

faq.question: Can I visit Bikini Atoll or the other nuclear test sites?
faq.answer: Only with permission. Bikini, Enewetak and Rongelap are governed by their atoll councils and the national government, and access depends on an authorized charter or liveaboard operating that season. Do not plan on turning up in Majuro and arranging it there. The approvals and the boat both need months of notice.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory?
faq.answer: No, it is not an entry requirement and nobody checks it. Given how far Majuro is from a full hospital, insurance that explicitly covers medical evacuation is the single most valuable thing to arrange before you fly, especially if you intend to dive.
